action: Confirmed via aspire.dev/NuGet docs for CommunityToolkit.Aspire.OllamaSharp 13.5.1-beta.736 that builder.AddOllamaApiClient(connectionName) alone registers only IOllamaApiClient/OllamaApiClient in DI -- it does NOT register Microsoft.Extensions.AI.IChatClient unless you either call AddOllamaSharpChatClient(connectionName) directly or chain .AddChatClient() off AddOllamaApiClient's return value. The existing code called builder.AddOllamaApiClient("qwen3:8b"); as a bare statement (return value discarded) and then separately did app.Services.GetRequiredService<IChatClient>() at line 14 -- exactly reproducing the reported System.InvalidOperationException, since nothing had ever registered IChatClient. Also found a second, related mismatch while fixing this: AppHost.cs adds the Ollama model resource as ollama.AddModel("model-orchestrator", "qwen3:8b") and references it via .WithReference(modelOrchestrator) with no name override, so the connection-string key Aspire injects into ProjectName.Runtime is "model-orchestrator" -- but Program.cs was passing the model TAG ("qwen3:8b") as the connection name instead of the actual Aspire resource name, which would have caused it to look up the wrong (or a missing) connection string once IChatClient registration was fixed. Corrected Program.cs to: builder.AddOllamaApiClient("model-orchestrator").AddChatClient(); -- fixing both the missing-registration crash and the connection-name mismatch in one edit. Left the display-only "qwen3:8b" model-name variable used later in the JSON responses unchanged, since that's just metadata, not a DI lookup key. Re-ran dotnet build .\ProjectName.slnx -m:1: Build succeeded, 0 Error(s), confirming .AddChatClient() resolves against the installed package version. Did not attempt a full aspire run to verify the Ollama container actually responds end-to-end (needs Docker + GPU + a model pull, out of scope for this cycle) -- recommended to the user as a follow-up manual check. Applied the fix directly to ProjectName.Runtime/Program.cs on disk but left it uncommitted, since that file already carries the user's own in-progress rewrite (old gRPC Program.cs -> new Aspire/Ollama Program.cs) and committing it here would bury that authorship under this trail's commit.
